perspective:
Cynthia’s available information:

- She is a teacher at a community center, teaching evening classes.
- Christina Gonzalez is her colleague and the marketing manager at the community center.
- Their relationship is professional; Cynthia knows they often disagree about program/marketing direction and are not personally close.
- In the staff meeting on upcoming semester marketing materials, Cynthia argues that traditional classes should be highlighted as the backbone of past success. She hears Christina argue for showcasing dynamic, interactive innovation and finding balance. Cynthia responds that traditional methods are proven, that shifting focus too drastically risks alienating long-time attendees, and that the marketing should play to the core audience’s value of structure and depth.
- Cynthia sees positive feedback from Christina’s last innovative marketing campaign. She asks Christina what she did differently. Christina tells her she used interactive elements and social media to create conversation and engagement. Cynthia says Christina managed to capture both depth and flash; Christina says they can blend new and old and learn from each other.
- Cynthia becomes less resistant to innovation, seeks Christina out, and proposes a joint pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. Christina agrees it could test how well their methods blend. Cynthia hopes it will enhance learning and draw a wider audience. They agree to outline specifics and implementation.
- Cynthia believes the pilot was a hit and wants to scale it up immediately. She tells Christina she will organize resources and set up a schedule. Christina says she will coordinate with marketing to publicize it. Cynthia is excited about the impact and agrees to keep momentum going.
- Cynthia receives overwhelmingly positive feedback and prepares a presentation to showcase the project’s success and advocate expanding the blended teaching approach to other centers. Christina offers help and says other centers could benefit. Cynthia says she is proud and views it as proof that blending methods was right.

Excluded: Christina’s private thoughts, narrator-only labels such as personality types/education/race unless directly self-known, and any events or information Cynthia did not observe, hear, or participate in.
